variables.name: kql_active_devices
variables.value: let window = 1d; DeviceInfo | where Timestamp >= ago(window) | where OnboardingStatus == 'Onboarded' | summarize TotalOnboarded = dcount(DeviceId)

variables.name: kql_new_alerts
variables.value: let window = 24h; AlertInfo | where Timestamp >= ago(window) | summarize NewAlerts = dcount(AlertId)

variables.name: kql_incidents_closed_SLA
variables.value: let window = 24h; let SLATime=24; SecurityIncident | where TimeGenerated >= ago(window) | where Status == 'Closed' | extend ResolutionTimeHours = datetime_diff('hour', ClosedTime, CreatedTime) | summarize SLA_Compliance = countif(ResolutionTimeHours <= SLATime), Total = count() | extend PIncidentsClosedInSLA = 100.0 * SLA_Compliance / Total | project PIncidentsClosedInSLA

variables.name: kql_incidents_by_severity_7d
variables.value: SecurityIncident | where TimeGenerated >= ago(7d) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated,*) by IncidentNumber | summarize High = countif(Severity == 'High'), Medium = countif(Severity == 'Medium'), Low = countif(Severity == 'Low')

variables.name: kql_new_discovered_apps
variables.value: CloudAppEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | summarize FirstSeenInWindow = min(Timestamp) by ApplicationId | where FirstSeenInWindow > ago(24h) | summarize UniqueApps = dcount(ApplicationId)

variables.name: kql_devices_no_telemetry
variables.value: let stale_window = 3d; DeviceInfo | where OnboardingStatus == 'Onboarded' | summarize LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceId | where LastSeen < ago(stale_window) | summarize DevicesWithoutTelemetry = dcount(DeviceId)

variables.name: kql_top3_users_alert_volume
variables.value: let window = 30d; AlertEvidence | where Timestamp >= ago(window) | where EntityType == 'User' | extend DisplayName = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields)['DisplayName']) | join kind=leftouter ( IdentityInfo | where Timestamp >= ago(30d) | summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by AccountUpn) on AccountUpn | summarize AlertCount = count() by AccountUpn, DisplayName, RiskLevel | project DisplayName, RiskLevel, AlertCount | top 3 by AlertCount desc

variables.name: kql_top3_devices_alert_volume
variables.value: let window = 30d; AlertEvidence | where Timestamp >= ago(window) and isnotempty(DeviceId) | summarize by AlertId, DeviceId, DeviceName | summarize Alerts=dcount(AlertId) by DeviceId, DeviceName | top 3 by Alerts desc

variables.name: kql_high_exposure_devices
variables.value: let window = 30d; DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(window) | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId | where ExposureLevel == 'High' | summarize HighExposureDevices = dcount(DeviceId)

variables.name: kql_top_cves_by_exposed_devices
variables.value: let N = 3; DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | summarize ExposedDevices = dcount(DeviceId) by CveId | top N by ExposedDevices desc | project CveId, ExposedDevices

variables.name: kql_pct_patchable_now
variables.value: let exposed = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | summarize by DeviceId; let patchable = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where isnotempty(RecommendedSecurityUpdateId) or isnotempty(RecommendedSecurityUpdate) | summarize by DeviceId; let total = toscalar(exposed | summarize Total=dcount(DeviceId)); let withUpdate = toscalar(patchable | summarize Patchable=dcount(DeviceId)); print ExposedDevices=total, WithRecommendedUpdate=withUpdate, PctWithRecommendedUpdate=iff(total == 0, 0.0, 100.0 * todouble(withUpdate) / todouble(total))

variables.name: kql_cves_public_exploits
variables.value: let tenant_cves = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | distinct CveId; DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB | where IsExploitAvailable == true | distinct CveId | join kind=inner tenant_cves on CveId | summarize CVEsWithPublicExploits = dcount(CveId)

variables.name: kql_devices_exposed_zeroDayNoFix
variables.value: let zeroDayNoFix = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where tostring(CveTags) has_any ('ZeroDay','NoSecurityUpdate') | distinct CveId; DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where CveId in (zeroDayNoFix) | summarize DevicesExposed = dcount(DeviceId)

variables.name: kql_new_high_sev_vulns_24h
variables.value: let window = 24h; let recent_high_kb = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilitiesKB | where isnotempty(PublishedDate) and PublishedDate >= ago(window) | where VulnerabilitySeverityLevel in ('High','Critical') | project CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, PublishedDate; DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where CveId in (recent_high_kb | project CveId) | distinct CveId | summarize NewHighSeverityCVEs = dcount(CveId)

variables.name: kql_top3_users_phishing_volume
variables.value: let window = 3d; EmailEvents | where Timestamp >= ago(window) | extend ThreatTypes = column_ifexists('ThreatTypes', dynamic([])) | where tostring(ThreatTypes) has 'Phish' | summarize PhishMessages = count() by RecipientEmailAddress | top 3 by PhishMessages desc

variables.name: kql_anomalous_cloud_activity_top5
variables.value: let window = 24h; CloudAppEvents | where Timestamp >= ago(window) | where isnotempty(UncommonForUser) and tostring(UncommonForUser) != '' and tostring(UncommonForUser) != '[]' | summarize Events=count() by AccountDisplayName, AccountId, Application | top 5 by Events desc

variables.name: kql_identity_risk_snapshot_sentinel
variables.value: IdentityInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by AccountUpn | summarize Compromised = countif(RiskStatus in ('ConfirmedCompromised', 'AtRisk')), HighRiskLevel = countif(RiskLevel == 'High'), MediumRiskLevel = countif(RiskLevel == 'Medium')

variables.name: kql_identity_risk_snapshot_basic
variables.value: IdentityInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by AccountUpn | summarize Compromised = 0, HighRiskLevel = countif(RiskLevel == 'High'), MediumRiskLevel = countif(RiskLevel == 'Medium')

body.PromptContent:
You are a vulnerability management advisor reviewing the daily exposure posture for a Microsoft 365 Defender tenant. Your task: identify the top 5 vulnerability and exposure risks the tenant should remediate TODAY. Focus EXCLUSIVELY on: - CVEs from the tenant's Advanced Hunting Top CVE list - Publicly exploitable vulnerabilities - Devices with High exposure level - Zero-day or no-fix vulnerabilities - Devices without telemetry as exposure blind spots Do NOT cover phishing, identity-only risks, SOC process issues, or general policy weaknesses — those are handled in other sections. Tenant KPI context: @{outputs('Compose_CopilotEvidence')} Tenant Top CVEs from Advanced Hunting: @{if(equals(actions('Condition_EnableMDE').status, 'Succeeded'), string(body('AH_TopCVEs')?['value']), 'N/A')} Instructions: - If the Top CVE list contains CVE IDs, at least 3 of the 5 items must reference a specific CVE ID from that list - Use the KPI values to explain urgency and blast radius (how many devices are affected) - Do not invent CVE IDs that are not present in the Top CVE list - If the Top CVE list is N/A or empty, derive the 5 items from the KPI metrics only - If a KPI metric is N/A or 0, skip it — do not fabricate a risk - Do not include URLs, markdown links, citations, references, footnotes, or source numbers such as [1], [[1]], (1), or URLs in parentheses. - Do not mention Microsoft Learn, documentation, or external sources. For each item: - Name the CVE ID or vulnerability risk - Reference the supporting metric or CVE list evidence - Explain in 1-2 sentences why it is dangerous in this environment - Give one specific remediation action using Defender Vulnerability Management, Intune, or MDE Keep language concise, technical but readable by a security manager. Output HTML only. No markdown, no backticks, no JSON, no introductory text, no text after the HTML. Return exactly this HTML structure:
  1. [CVE ID or risk name] — [supporting evidence]
    [Why it matters in this environment — 1-2 sentences]
    Remediation: [Specific action with tool name]

body.PromptContent:
You are a Chief Information Security Officer advisor writing a daily security posture briefing for a Microsoft 365 tenant. Your task: evaluate the overall security health of this tenant across all product areas and produce a concise executive overview — not a list of remediation steps, but an assessment of where the tenant stands today. Audience: IT director or security manager. They want to know if the environment is healthy, degrading, or under active threat — not what the SOC should do step by step. Full tenant KPI context: @{outputs('Compose_CopilotEvidence')} Structure your response as: 1. Overall posture rating: Healthy / Needs Attention / At Risk — with a one-sentence justification 2. Top 3 signals driving the rating (pick the most significant cross-product indicators) 3. One area that is stable or improved (if visible in the data) 4. One area to watch in the next 24h Rules: - Do not list remediation steps or SOC tasks — those are covered in separate sections - Do not repeat every metric — synthesize and evaluate - If data is N/A for a product, note it is not monitored and exclude it from the rating - Keep each point to 1-2 sentences maximum - If there is no major issue, say the environment appears stable and mention the top area to continue monitoring - Do not include URLs, markdown links, citations, references, footnotes, or source numbers such as [1], [[1]], (1), or URLs in parentheses. - Do not mention Microsoft Learn, documentation, or external sources. - Tone: calm, authoritative, business-friendly - Output HTML only — no markdown, no backticks, no JSON, no text before or after the HTML Return exactly this HTML structure:

Overall posture: [Healthy / Needs Attention / At Risk] — [One-sentence justification]

Key signals

  1. [Signal] — [1-2 sentence evaluation]
  2. [Signal] — [1-2 sentence evaluation]
  3. [Signal] — [1-2 sentence evaluation]

Stable area: [What looks good or unchanged]

Watch in next 24h: [One area to monitor]

body.PromptContent:
You are a SOC Team Lead writing the daily operational briefing for security analysts and incident responders. Your task: identify the top 3 active risk themes from incidents, alerts, and identity signals that the SOC team should investigate or respond to TODAY. Focus EXCLUSIVELY on: - Active incidents (high/medium/low severity counts and SLA compliance) - Identity compromise signals (compromised users, high/medium risk users) - Phishing and email threats - Anomalous cloud app activity - Cross-product attack chains visible in the data Do NOT cover CVEs, device patches, vulnerability remediation, or executive posture evaluation — those are handled in separate sections. Tenant operational data: @{outputs('Compose_CopilotEvidence')} A risk theme is an observable pattern in active incidents or alerts — not a generic category. Name only themes supported by the data. For each theme: - Name the specific pattern observed - State which data signals support it (reference the metric and value) - Explain the operational risk in 1-2 sentences - Give one specific SOC action naming the tool and analyst step (e.g. triage in Defender XDR incident queue, run KQL hunt in Sentinel, review Entra ID risky sign-ins) Rules: - If fewer than 3 distinct themes are visible in the data, return only real ones and note the rest are not observed today - Do not invent themes from N/A or zero metrics - Do not include URLs, markdown links, citations, references, footnotes, or source numbers such as [1], [[1]], (1), or URLs in parentheses. - Do not mention Microsoft Learn, documentation, or external sources. - Output HTML only — no markdown, no backticks, no JSON, no text before or after the HTML Return exactly this HTML structure:
  1. [Theme name] — [supporting metric]: [value]
    Operational risk: [1-2 sentences]
    SOC action: [Specific tool + analyst step]
